clue.text: Current tribute defends quiet expertise

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for alternating current

indicators.note: defends means the tribute word stands around and shields the quiet word

parts.note: a compliment is a tribute paid to someone
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: An electrical tribute somehow protects a quiet person's skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment is a skill or proficiency gained by practice, so it can stand for expertise.

clue.text: Later instruction from TUC holding journalist in high regard

indicators.note: in means that combined unit sits inside the high regard word

parts.note: adulation is excessive admiration, high regard

indicators.note: holding means the TUC letters wrap around the journalist

parts.note: taken as written: the Trades Union Congress
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Union leaders admire a reporter's training scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Later' looks like a time word for the surface, but it means later in life: schooling for grown-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult education is teaching for grown-ups, instruction taken up later in life than school.

clue.text: Constant bids for funds

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics
offers are bids

explanation.surface: Steady bidding for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are chests for valuables, and by extension the funds or treasury of an organisation.

clue.text: Chairman's supporter avoids area that's wet

indicators.note: avoids means the area letter is kept out

parts.note: a Maoist supports Chairman Mao

explanation.surface: A political follower steers clear of a soggy patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet or damp, a close synonym.

clue.text: Call up sponsor to be collected

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the call word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to dial is to call on the phone
to back is to sponsor

explanation.surface: Phoning a backer to be picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' suggests being fetched; here it means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected person is calm and composed; laid-back means relaxed and unflustered.

clue.text: Distinguished archbishop is revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the archbishop plus is reads backwards

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noted churchman turns out to be a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: LANG plus IS reversed gives SIGNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means notable or striking, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Big Eddy, top performer, clutches large mike

indicators.note: clutches means the top performer word grips the large letter

parts.note: a maestro is a master performer
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A star called Eddy grabs a big microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name; it is a swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, an eddy on a grand scale.

clue.text: Don't look after injured leg caught in trap

indicators.note: in means the injured leg and caught letter go inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: injured means the leg letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An animal with a hurt leg is caught in a trap and left untended.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to care for it, an idiom-style imperative definition.

clue.text: Used dinner hour misguidedly, turning out thus?

definitions.text: Used dinner hour misguidedly, turning out thus?

indicators.note: misguidedly means wrongly directed, so the letters are sent into the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone wasted their lunch break and ended up going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both makes and describes the answer: misuse the dinner hour and you end up unfed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undernourished means lacking enough food, the result of not eating at mealtime.

clue.text: Reliable Blue Berets fit into cast

parts.note: United Nations peacekeepers wear blue berets, so they are the UN

indicators.note: into means the fit word is put inside the cast word

parts.note: to fling is to cast or throw
AI (A1) means in first-class condition, fit

explanation.surface: Dependable UN peacekeepers are being fitted into a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning in top condition, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfailing never lets you down, which is exactly what reliable means.

clue.text: Drive, say, all but disappeared

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an example

indicators.note: all but means everything except the final letter is kept

parts.note: gone means disappeared

explanation.surface: A car journey, for instance, has almost vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to urge or push someone forward, the sense of drive as in impel.

clue.text: Deal with danger, losing height

indicators.note: losing means the height letter drops out of the danger word

parts.note: a threat is a danger

explanation.surface: Handling a hazard by getting it down from a high place.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or person is to handle or manage it, which is to deal with it.

clue.text: Support at the front from top officers, before one retreats

parts.note: the brass, or top brass, are senior officers

indicators.note: retreats means the before word and the one word go into reverse together

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Senior officers back a frontal attack while one soldier withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support at the front' sounds military, matching the officers, but it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra supports the bust, which is at the front of the body, so this is a witty description of the garment.

clue.text: Detective's words before meal are degrading

definitions.note: used as a noun: a degrading, a debasement, which is a disgrace

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; with the apostrophe S, DI'S
grace is the prayer said before eating

explanation.surface: A police officer says grace at dinner, and it is humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace is a shameful loss of standing, a debasement of someone's honour.

clue.text: It's feasible dealing with with boxer's idiosyncrasy

parts.note: RE means concerning, dealing with
Muhammad Ali is the boxer; with the apostrophe S, ALI'S
a tic is a habitual quirk or mannerism

explanation.surface: Coping with a fighter's personal quirk is practicable.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'with' is printed so; the second is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic plan is achievable and practical, in other words feasible.

clue.text: Surrealist backed enthralling Republican

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the backed words hold the Republican letter

parts.note: to have bet on a horse is to have backed it

explanation.surface: An artist supported a Republican politician who fascinated him.
explanation.walkthrough: André Breton was the French writer who founded Surrealism.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton wrote the Surrealist Manifesto in 1924 and led the movement, so he is the archetypal surrealist.

clue.text: Swimmers turn red if energy rises internally

indicators.note: internally means they sit inside the turn red word

parts.note: to blush is to turn red

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the if and energy letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fish go red when their energy climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluefish are predatory ocean fish; the name serves as singular and plural, so swimmers fits.

clue.text: Uncaring, cold as usual, snubbing our lot

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

indicators.note: snubbing means ignoring, so the our-lot word is left out

parts.note: taken as written
us is our lot, the group we belong to

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent and chilly, as ever, ignores our group.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual attitude is offhand and unconcerned, so casual can mean uncaring.

clue.text: What's picked up in disorderly creches?

definitions.text: What's picked up in disorderly creches?

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters of creches are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking what you'd hear in an unruly nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the shrill sound you hear in an unruly nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a shrill piercing cry, the sort heard from children running riot.

clue.text: A medic wearing jumper with posh torch

indicators.note: wearing means the jumper is put on around the A and the medic

parts.note: a flea is a jumping insect
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A doctor in a sweater, accompanied by someone upper-class, carries a torch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as a doctor might wear, but it is the flea.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of thick wicks dipped in wax.

clue.text: Charge for altering test run

indicators.note: altering means changing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fee for changing a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to entrust it to them.

clue.text: Scrap odd parts of tours on isle to avoid current

indicators.note: odd parts of means take letters in the odd positions only

parts.note: odd letters of tours: first, third and fifth

indicators.note: to avoid means the current letter is left out of the word isle

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Cancel some of the island tours to stay clear of the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: TUS from tours, then SLE from isle without I.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight or scuffle, and a tussle is a vigorous struggle.

clue.text: Trade union offensive limiting mine corruption

indicators.note: limiting means the offensive word bounds the mine on both sides

parts.note: rude means offensive
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A union's campaign to restrict a colliery ends in corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is depravity or baseness of character, a moral corruption.

clue.text: African socialist utopia recalled to some extent

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A socialist dream is partly remembered by an African.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa, so a Tutsi is an African.

clue.text: Article's followed by thank-you letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is a British colloquial thank-you

explanation.surface: A news piece is followed up by a note of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Finished twentieth originally in the Open

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: originally means only the start of the next word is taken

parts.note: first letter of twentieth

explanation.surface: A golfer finished twentieth in the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the Open as the golf tournament; as the definition it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden, so it matches open.

clue.text: Small fish attack pond plant

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
the pike is a predatory freshwater fish
to rush is to charge at, attack

explanation.surface: A little fish goes on the attack among the pond weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike-rush is a sedge of wet ground and pond margins, with leafless stems topped by a single spike.

clue.text: Easily scared, Kitchener ached after surgery

indicators.note: surgery rearranges the body, so the letters come out rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Lord Kitchener was frightened, aching after his operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener was the British field marshal of the recruiting poster, an unlikely coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken-hearted means timid or cowardly, frightened by little.
